question: Design a service for real-time remote monitoring and analytics for distributed commercial greenhouse facilities. POST /greenhouses/{greenhouseId}/sensors/data ingests sensor data (temperature, humidity, soil moisture) from millions of sensors across numerous facilities; GET /greenhouses/{greenhouseId}/dashboard returns a real-time analytics dashboard. Constraints: continuous ingestion and processing of data streams from millions of sensors; near-real-time processing with guaranteed consistency and traceability for auditing; high availability plus robust monitoring and alerting for system health and data anomalies.
constraints: continuous ingestion from millions of sensors
monitoring and alerting for health and anomalies
traps: no fixed throughput or latency figure can be promised without the fleet's actual rates
no cloud service level agreement may be stated as fact

history.q: Design a chat service for one-to-one and group conversations with message history, delivery receipts and presence for 50 million daily users.
history.a: I would keep connections on a websocket gateway tier and fan messages out per conversation, with history stored in a partitioned log so receipts and ordering stay consistent. Presence would live in memory with a short expiry and be served from a dedicated tier.

question: And what happens to that retention if the compliance team requires seven years?

history.q: How is our telemetry topic partitioned, and how long do we keep raw sensor readings?
history.a: The telemetry topic is keyed by greenhouseId and has 48 partitions. Raw readings are kept for 400 days, and the aggregator writes 5-second rollups that are kept for five years.
